title: Manipulating osa-MIR156f Expression by D18 Promoter to Regulate Plant Architecture and Yield Traits
author: Liu, Su, et al.
materials: O. sativa spp. japonica cv. Nipponbare

After the seasonal rice harvest, old roots were cut off from the rice stubble and the rice stubble was replanted in soil. After culturing for 7 days, the number of the regenerated roots was counted. A TTC (2,3,5-triphenyte-trazolium chloride) method [55] was employed to analyze the root activity of regenerated roots. TTC (Sigma) was dissolved in 100 mM sodium phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) to a final concentration of 0.6% (w/v). Root segments about 1 cm to 3 cm in length, were collected and washed with sterile water for 10 min. The root segments were transferred into 1 mL of TTC solution and incubated for 1 h at 37 °C in the dark. The TTC solution was removed and the root segments were rinsed once with deionized water. For the extraction process, the root segments were incubated overnight at room temperature in 2 mL of 95% (v/v) ethanol. The reduction of TTC was expressed as the absorbance of the extracted solutions at 520 nm in a spectrophotometer. Three independent biological replicates were analyzed.

steps.title: GUS staining of transgenic tissues
steps.instruction: Perform GUS staining on five osa‑MIR156fpro::GUS transgenic plants using the specified tissues and reagents.

substeps.instruction: Collect tissues at the indicated developmental stages: leaves and roots at seedling, tillering and heading stages; shoot apexes at 3‑week seedling stage; axillary buds at tillering and heading stages; basal nodes at tillering and heading stages; stem segments at stem elongation and flowering stages; spikes at heading stage; and stamens at flowering stage.
Wash the harvested tissues three times with 100 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.0).

Incubate the washed tissues in the staining solution composed of 100 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.0), 10 mM EDTA, 2 mM 5‑bromo‑4‑chloro‑3‑indolyl‑β‑D‑GlcA, 5 mM K₄Fe(CN)₆, 5 mM K₃Fe(CN)₆, and 0.2 % Triton X‑100 for 24 h at 37 °C.
After staining, soak the tissues in 90 % ethanol for 24–48 h, then observe the GUS signal.

steps.title: Prepare rice extract for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Extract strigolactones from rice tissue and prepare the sample for LC‑MS/MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Grind approximately 200 mg of rice tissue in liquid nitrogen and transfer the fine powder to a 2.0 mL vial.
Add 1.0 mL HPLC‑grade acetone (Tedia), stir in an ultrasonic bath, and store the mixture overnight at –20 °C.
Centrifuge the suspension at 15,200 g for 10 min; collect the supernatant.
Vacuum‑dry the supernatant using an RCT‑60 concentrator (Jouan).
Dissolve the dried residue in 300 µL HPLC‑grade methanol (Merck).
Pass the solution through a Waters Sep‑Pak C18 cartridge; elute the cartridge with 1,500 µL of 80 % methanol.
Vacuum‑dry the eluate again, then re‑dissolve in 50 µL of 80 % methanol.
Inject 10 µL of the final solution into the LC‑MS/MS system (Shimadzu LC‑MS/MS 8030 plus).

steps.title: Run LC gradient for SL analysis
steps.instruction: Separate strigolactones on a Shim‑pack XR‑ODSI column using a defined gradient program.

substeps.instruction: Install a 2.0 mm i.d. × 75 mm Shim‑pack XR‑ODSI column (2.2 µm) and set the column temperature to 40 °C.
Prepare mobile phase A (0.1 % v/v aqueous formic acid) and mobile phase B (100 % v/v acetonitrile).
Apply the following gradient (time / % A / % B): 0 min / 90 % A / 10 % B, 12 min / 0 % A / 100 % B, 13 min / 0 % A / 100 % B, 14 min / 90 % A / 10 % B.
Set the flow rate to 0.25 mL·min⁻¹.

steps.title: Configure MS for MRM detection
steps.instruction: Set the mass spectrometer to multiple‑reaction‑monitoring mode for quantifying strigolactones.

substeps.instruction: Select electrospray ionization in positive mode and enable MRM.
Use 5‑dexoxystrigol (5‑DS, Strigolab) as the external standard.
Set nebulizing gas flow to 1.5 L·min⁻¹, drying gas flow to 12 L·min⁻¹, desolvation temperature to 200 °C, and heat block temperature to 500 °C.
Program quadrupole 1 pre‑bias to –17 eV, quadrupole 3 pre‑bias to –22 eV, and collision energy to –17 eV.
Monitor the transition m/z 331.1 → 216.2 for 5‑DS.
Calculate strigolactone concentrations from a calibration curve generated with 5‑DS standards (R² = 0.9967); analyze three independent biological replicates.

steps.title: Regenerate roots and count number
steps.instruction: After harvest, cut old roots from rice stubble, replant the stubble in soil, grow for 7 days, then count regenerated roots.

steps.title: Perform TTC root activity assay
steps.instruction: Determine the activity of regenerated roots using the TTC reduction method.

substeps.instruction: Prepare TTC solution by dissolving TTC (Sigma) in 100 mM sodium phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) to a final concentration of 0.6 % w/v.
Collect root segments 1–3 cm long, wash them with sterile water for 10 min.
Transfer the segments to 1 mL TTC solution and incubate for 1 h at 37 °C in the dark.
Remove the TTC solution and rinse the segments once with deionized water.
Extract the reduced TTC by incubating the segments overnight at room temperature in 2 mL 95 % (v/v) ethanol.
Measure the absorbance of the ethanol extract at 520 nm using a spectrophotometer; perform three independent biological replicates.
